chapters.title: Bringing JavaScript and hardware together
chapters.summary: Hardware, JavaScript and toolkit concepts. Build circuits and write your own code in the blank lab; the chapter has no runnable source project.

chapters.title: Embarking on hardware with Arduino
chapters.summary: Original Johnny-Five blink and stop programs run on the AVR Uno simulation. The optional Arduino C++ sketch remains linked; editing/uploading C++ is outside this JavaScript runtime.

chapters.title: How to build circuits
chapters.summary: Breadboard connections, DC resistance, voltage/current measurements, and series/parallel circuits have circuit models. Transients, component damage and every real-world electrical effect are outside the model.

chapters.title: Projects without wires
chapters.summary: Tessel LED, GPIO, weather and rover sources are available through labelled virtual APIs; selected web-server APIs use an in-memory preview. Wireless configuration and native Tessel hardware execution remain external.

chapters.title: Building with Node.js and tiny computers
chapters.summary: Pi/BeagleBone GPIO, virtual sysfs files, selected wiring-pi/Raspi/BeagleBone APIs and weather web previews are available. The original shell blink uses a bounded virtual echo/sleep/GPIO-filesystem interpreter. Native Bash, OS/addons and actual TCP networking remain external.

chapters.title: In the cloud, in the browser, and beyond
chapters.summary: The cloud weather program has a virtual local-server path; Puck LED/doorbell sources have explicit virtual Bluetooth serial models. Cloud provisioning, Docker deployment, physical Bluetooth pairing and radios remain external. Original Puck web button/doorbell flows, LED pulse, CHIME parsing and bundled audio loading have browser checks; complete prepared wiring remains a separate review.

exercises.note: Original multi-file weather dashboard displays 77.00 F and 1013.25 mbar in the browser iframe through the in-memory server API bridge. Prepared circuit wiring and hardware/native deployment are separate from this program check. The weather program and web interface can run locally with virtual APIs. Resin/balena account, Docker deployment, device provisioning and cloud management are outside this browser model.

Original Puck browser ON/OFF buttons control virtual LED1 through the explicit connection shim. Prepared circuit wiring and hardware/native deployment are separate from this program check. Original browser buttons send LED1.set/reset through an explicit virtual Puck connection. This demonstrates the JavaScript workflow without a Bluetooth radio, physical pairing or native Puck interpreter.

Original doorbell HTML and PuckChime.js receive virtual BTN/CHIME text, emit a 250 ms LED1 pulse and load the inlined original audio asset in a real browser. Prepared circuit wiring and hardware/native deployment are separate from this program check. Original PuckChime.js sends reset/button-watch code through a virtual Puck connection. BTN rising events emit CHIME text and LED flashes. Browser sound uses the bundled example audio; no Bluetooth radio or pairing is emulated.
